drugs.name: Belimumab (Benlysta)
drugs.mechanism: Binds and neutralizes soluble BAFF, reducing B cell survival and autoantibody production
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2011 (SLE), 2020 (lupus nephritis)
drugs.efficacy: SRI-4 response rate ~43-58% at 52 weeks

drugs.name: Anifrolumab (Saphnelo)
drugs.mechanism: Blocks type I interferon receptor, suppressing the IFN gene signature
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2021 (moderate to severe SLE)
drugs.efficacy: BICLA response rate ~47% vs 30% placebo at 52 weeks (TULIP-2)

drugs.name: Voclosporin (Lupkynis)
drugs.mechanism: Calcineurin inhibitor; blocks T cell activation and podocyte stabilization in the kidney
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2021 (lupus nephritis)
drugs.efficacy: Complete renal response ~41% vs 23% placebo at 52 weeks (AURORA-1)

drugs.name: Hydroxychloroquine (Plaquenil)
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits endosomal acidification, blocking TLR7/9 activation and reducing type I IFN production
drugs.approval: Standard of care for all SLE patients
drugs.efficacy: Reduces flares by ~50%, improves survival, reduces thrombosis and organ damage

drugs.name: Mycophenolate Mofetil (CellCept)
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits de novo purine synthesis, selectively suppressing lymphocyte proliferation
drugs.approval: Widely used off-label for lupus nephritis; standard of care
drugs.efficacy: Comparable to cyclophosphamide for lupus nephritis induction (ALMS trial)

drugs.name: Cyclophosphamide (Cytoxan)
drugs.mechanism: Alkylates DNA, causing cell death in rapidly dividing cells including lymphocytes
drugs.approval: Reserved for severe organ-threatening lupus (nephritis, CNS, pulmonary)
drugs.efficacy: Gold standard for severe lupus nephritis; limited by toxicity

drugs.name: Rituximab (Rituxan)
drugs.mechanism: Depletes CD20+ B cells via ADCC, complement-dependent cytotoxicity, and apoptosis
drugs.approval: Off-label for refractory SLE (failed RCTs LUNAR and EXPLORER but widely used clinically)
drugs.efficacy: Used in refractory disease; registry data supports efficacy despite negative RCTs

drugs.name: Prednisone (Corticosteroids)
drugs.mechanism: Broad immunosuppression via NF-κB inhibition, reduced cytokine production, and induction of apoptosis in immune cells
drugs.approval: Mainstay of acute SLE management
drugs.efficacy: Rapid disease control but significant long-term toxicity; goal is ≤7.5mg/day maintenance

drugs.name: Tacrolimus (Prograf)
drugs.mechanism: Calcineurin inhibitor; blocks T cell activation via NFAT inhibition
drugs.approval: Off-label for lupus nephritis (especially in Asian populations)
drugs.efficacy: Non-inferior to mycophenolate in some Asian lupus nephritis trials

drugs.name: Azathioprine (Imuran)
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits purine synthesis, reducing lymphocyte proliferation
drugs.approval: Maintenance therapy for lupus nephritis; steroid-sparing agent
drugs.efficacy: Effective for maintenance after induction; reduces relapse rates

drugs.name: Baricitinib (Olumiant)
drugs.mechanism: JAK1/2 inhibitor blocking type I IFN, IL-6, and other cytokine signaling
drugs.approval: Phase 3 trials in SLE (SLE-BRAVE I & II); mixed results
drugs.efficacy: Phase 2 positive; Phase 3 SLE-BRAVE-I met primary endpoint, SLE-BRAVE-II did not

drugs.name: Obinutuzumab (Gazyva)
drugs.mechanism: Type II anti-CD20 antibody with enhanced B cell depletion vs rituximab
drugs.approval: Phase 3 in lupus nephritis (REGENCY trial, positive results 2024)
drugs.efficacy: Superior to placebo for lupus nephritis in REGENCY trial (presented ACR 2024)

drugs.name: Acalabrutinib (Calquence)
drugs.mechanism: Highly selective, irreversible second-generation BTK inhibitor with reduced off-target kinase inhibition vs ibrutinib
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2017 (CLL), 2019 (MCL)
drugs.efficacy: Improved selectivity profile with reduced cardiovascular and bleeding events vs ibrutinib

drugs.name: Avacopan (Tavneos)
drugs.mechanism: Selective C5a receptor antagonist that blocks C5a-mediated neutrophil activation, migration, and adhesion
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2021 (ANCA-associated vasculitis)
drugs.efficacy: Superior to prednisone taper for sustained remission in ANCA vasculitis (ADVOCATE trial)

drugs.name: Cyclosporine (Neoral / Sandimmune)
drugs.mechanism: Binds cyclophilin and inhibits calcineurin, blocking NFAT dephosphorylation and IL-2 transcription
drugs.approval: Off-label for lupus nephritis; widely used in transplantation and autoimmune disease
drugs.efficacy: Effective in lupus nephritis, especially as steroid-sparing agent and in membranous lupus nephritis

drugs.name: Dimethyl Fumarate (Tecfidera)
drugs.mechanism: Activates Nrf2 antioxidant pathway and inhibits NF-κB nuclear translocation, reducing proinflammatory cytokine production
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2013 (multiple sclerosis)
drugs.efficacy: Reduces relapse rate by ~44-53% in relapsing MS; immunomodulatory effects demonstrated

drugs.name: Iscalimab (CFZ533 / anti-CD40)
drugs.mechanism: Blocks CD40-CD40L interaction, preventing T cell-dependent B cell activation and germinal center formation
drugs.approval: Phase 2 in Sjögren’s syndrome and renal transplantation (investigational)
drugs.efficacy: Promising Phase 2 results in Sjögren's syndrome; blocks T-B costimulation without platelet effects of anti-CD40L

drugs.name: Ravulizumab (Ultomiris)
drugs.mechanism: Long-acting monoclonal antibody that binds C5 and blocks cleavage into C5a and C5b-9 (MAC)
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2018 (PNH), 2019 (atypical HUS)
drugs.efficacy: Non-inferior to eculizumab with extended dosing interval (every 8 weeks vs every 2 weeks)

drugs.name: Rozanolixizumab (Rystiggo)
drugs.mechanism: Blocks FcRn, reducing IgG recycling and accelerating pathogenic IgG degradation
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2023 (generalized myasthenia gravis)
drugs.efficacy: Significant improvement in MG-ADL scores in Phase 3 (MycarinG trial)

drugs.name: Tofacitinib (Xeljanz)
drugs.mechanism: Pan-JAK inhibitor (JAK1 > JAK3 > JAK2) that broadly blocks cytokine signaling through JAK-STAT pathways
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2012 (RA), 2017 (PsA), 2018 (UC)
drugs.efficacy: Effective across multiple autoimmune diseases; SLE-specific trials not conducted
